result.title: Why 3D Reconstruction Breaks Down on Under-Ice AUV Video, and How to Predict It
result.comment: Short paper presented at the 2nd Workshop on Marine Vision, ECCV 2026, Malmö, Sweden, September 8, 2026. Published on OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=6wgkZngDjW
result.summary: Reconstruction of 3D structures using under-ice AUV video footage has been inaccurate, although it is not certain whether this is due to shortcomings in the methods or an inherent deficiency of the capture system. We test four different models for reconstruction on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video (Icefin, Kamb Ice Stream): classical feature matching SfM, differentiable photometric splatting, volumetric depth fusion, and a pose-free feed-forward foundation model. All four fail, each in a distinct way: near-total registration yielding almost no structure, geometrically broken output despite healthy photometric metrics, a persistent coverage artifact, and unstable cross-chunk scale. We show that all four are consistent with the same capture regime, a small camera-baseline-to-scene-depth ratio. Following our analysis, we propose a detection system that flags this type of failure in minutes, rather than hours of wasted compute.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在同一段南极冰下 AUV 视频上对比四种三维重建方法（特征匹配 SfM、可微分光度 splatting、体深度融合、无位姿前馈基础模型），发现它们全部失败且失败方式各异，并归因于相机基线相对场景深度过小的采集条件，进而提出可在数分钟内标记该类失败的检测系统。
AI.relevance_reason: 远域（冰下 AUV 视觉）的失败诊断揭示「光度指标健康但几何结构已损坏」的代理指标失配，可能启发 LVR 中对 latent 相似度指标与视觉证据是否真正保留的区分，以及证据不足时及早停止后续计算；联系仍属推测，可供核查。
